WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of her
She heard “of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD”, and came to test him “with hard questions”. 1 Kings 10:1
“She communed with him of all that was in her heart. And Solomon told her all her questions.” 1 Kings 10:2–3

“It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom. Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me.” 1 Kings 10:6–7
“Blessed be the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel.” 1 Kings 10:9
“So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.” 1 Kings 10:13
Jesus: “The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it … and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.” Matthew 12:42
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
She came because of Solomon's fame “concerning the name of the LORD”. 1 Kings 10:1
She blessed “the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee”. 1 Kings 10:9
She saw “the house that he had built”, and his ascent to the house of the LORD. 1 Kings 10:4–5
Gifts on both sides: her gold, spices and stones; his gifts “of his royal bounty”. 1 Kings 10:10 1 Kings 10:13
From the text1 Kings 10 places her visit amid Solomon's trade by sea and his gold; Kings records no treaty with her. 1 Kings 10:11 1 Kings 10:14
“Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee.” 1 Kings 10:8
“There came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.” 1 Kings 10:10

PLACED BY SOLOMON'S REIGN (THIELE, AS REVISED BY MCFALL AND YOUNG)
No years given[1]
Her visit is undated. It falls within Solomon's reign, 971–932 BC in Young's table; 1 Kings tells it after the temple and the palace were finished.
Ethiopia
The Kebra Nagast (Arabic version AD 1314–1344)
The Ethiopian tradition makes her Makeda, queen of Ethiopia.[32]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives her name, her husband or family, or the length of her reign.
1 Kings 10 does not say where Sheba lay.
Scripture says nothing of a son by Solomon; that is the Kebra Nagast's tradition.
Scripture does not say what she did after she went home.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textScripture never gives her name. “Makeda” and “Balkis” come from much later traditions; this page does not use them as her name. 1 Kings 10:1
From the textJesus calls her “the queen of the south” who “came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon”. Matthew 12:42 Luke 11:31
From the textShe is called a queen and comes and goes with her own servants; Scripture names no king beside her. 1 Kings 10:1 1 Kings 10:13
